title: "Decomposition and uncertainty"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
# These analyses train models and resample hundreds of times, so the chunks
# are shown but not run when the site is built.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

A normalised series tells you what remains once the weather is averaged out.
This article goes two steps further. It splits the series into its drivers,
and it puts error bars on the normalised estimate. It reuses `df_prep`,
`model`, `covariates` and `predictors` from
[Weather normalisation, step by step](normalisation-workflow.html).

```{r}
library(normet)

covariates <- c("ws", "wd", "temp", "RH", "atmos_pres", "blh", "tcc", "tp", "ssrd")
predictors <- c(covariates, "date_unix", "day_julian", "weekday", "hour")
build   <- nm_build_model(my1, target = "NO2", covariates = predictors)
df_prep <- build$df_prep
model   <- build$model
```

## Decomposition

`nm_decompose()` separates the series into the components attributable to
different drivers:

- `method = "emission"` isolates the contribution of the time-based features
  (trend, season, weekday, hour) from the weather-driven part.
- `method = "meteorology"` gives the contribution of each weather variable,
  or of named groups of them (`groups =`), to the target.

```{r}
df_emi <- nm_decompose(method = "emission",    df = df_prep, target = "value",
                       model = model, n_samples = 300)
df_met <- nm_decompose(method = "meteorology", df = df_prep, target = "value",
                       model = model, n_samples = 300)

nm_plot_decomposition_stack(df_emi)
```

`nm_decom_emi()` and `nm_decom_met()` are the two methods' own functions.
`nm_decompose()` dispatches to them. For a station network,
`nm_decompose_multisite()` runs the decomposition once per site (see
[Multi-site pipelines and caching](multisite-caching.html)).

## Uncertainty ensemble

`nm_do_all_unc()` trains `n_models` models, each with its own seed, normalises
with each, and summarises the spread across the ensemble:

```{r}
unc <- nm_do_all_unc(
  df            = my1,
  target        = "NO2",
  covariates    = predictors,
  resample_vars = covariates,
  n_models      = 10,
  n_samples     = 300
)
head(unc$res)     # observed, one normalised_<seed> column per member, then
                  # mean, std, median, lower_bound, upper_bound, weighted
unc$mod_stats     # performance metrics of every ensemble member
```

`nm_decompose_uncertainty()` answers a related question: how much of a
de-weathered estimate's total spread is due to the weather resampling, and how
much to the form of the model? Its result has `print()`, `summary()`, `plot()`
and `as.data.frame()` methods.

## Trends in the normalised series

Once a series is normalised, these functions test and describe its trend:

- `nm_trend()`: the Mann-Kendall test and the Theil-Sen slope. Where the
  residuals are autocorrelated, a block-bootstrap interval is added.
- `nm_trend_breaks()`: where the trend breaks. Each segment gets its own
  Theil-Sen slope.
- `nm_mann_kendall()` and `nm_theil_sen()`: the two tests on their own.

See their reference pages for the arguments and the output.
